newsitem.title: USA: Bunning announces run for Kentucky Senate seat.
newsitem.headline: Bunning announces run for Kentucky Senate seat.

text.p: Republican Representative Jim Bunning, a Hall of Fame baseball pitcher with a conservative record in Congress, announced his candidacy on Tuesday for retiring Democrat Wendell Ford's Senate seat.

Bunning, 65, was first elected to the House in 1986 from the northern Kentucky district dominated by suburbs stretching from Louisville to communities opposite Cincinnati, Ohio. He declared his candidacy at news conferences held across the state, including this town near Cincinnati.

Bunning has been a strong proponent of a balanced federal budget and spending cuts and an opponent of tax increases. Prior to entering politics, he was an investment broker and before that he spent 22 years as a pitcher for several major league teams, setting a record for hitting batters with pitched balls.

The 72-year-old Ford, who announced March 10 that he would retire after his fourth term expires, said he believed Bunning was "so far right, out at the fringes" that he would be relatively easy to beat.

Kentucky Democratic Representative Scotty Baesler also plans to run for Ford's seat. Other potential Democratic contenders include Lt. Gov. Steve Henry and state Attorney General Ben Chandler. Republicans now have a 55-45 majority in the Senate.
